title: Greet with better
hookLine: when greeted, return a better greeting or the same (4:86)
carry: add the mercy and the blessings
last: MAKE IT ABOUT WHAT, NOT WHO.

lines: A LITTLE MORE THAN YOU GAVE.
cards: Someone texts you: good morning! You reply: morning. Someone at work says: hope your weekend was great.
You say: yep, you too. Nothing wrong with it. Now picture a reply with a little more than you were given: a name, a question, a real wish.
It lands differently. An-Nisa, between laws about war and peace, stops to give a rule about something as small as hello.

teach.b: Here's 4:86 in Pickthall's words: "When ye are greeted with a greeting, greet ye with a better than it or return it. Lo! Allah taketh count of all things."
The word for greeting is tahiyyah, from the root of hayah, life: at its root, a greeting is a wish for someone's life. The rule has two levels. The minimum: give back what you were given.
The better way: add to it. The Muslim greeting shows how. As-salamu 'alaykum: peace be upon you.
The better reply adds a layer: wa 'alaykum as-salam wa rahmatullah, and upon you be peace, and God's mercy. Better still: wa barakatuh, and His blessings. A hadith in Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi tells it.
A man said as-salamu 'alaykum, and the Prophet ﷺ answered him and said: ten.
Another added wa rahmatullah: twenty. A third added wa barakatuh: thirty. Commentators explain: ten good deeds for each piece.

And a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari takes the custom back to the beginning. When God created Adam, He told him to go and greet a group of angels and listen to their answer, because it would be the greeting of his children.
Adam said as-salamu 'alaykum. The angels replied: as-salamu 'alayka wa rahmatullah.

teach.h: GREET YE WITH A BETTER THAN IT.
teach.b: In the story, the first greeting is answered with better. And the verse's last line: God takes count of all things. In the verse, even a hello is counted.

how: Muslims greet each other with as-salamu 'alaykum and are taught to return it with at least the same, and ideally more: wa 'alaykum as-salam wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh.

o: a greeting: at its root, a wish for life
the prayer said over food before eating
a formal bow you make to your elders

games.q: greet with better — tap the pairs.
p: a greeting, a wish for life

s: returning a greeting with exactly the same words breaks the rule
the verse says greet with better, or return it: the same is the minimum.
in the hadith, the fullest greeting earned thirty
ten, twenty, thirty: one for each added piece.
the verse says small things like greetings don't count
it ends: God takes count of all things.

games.q: you're Adam. God tells you to greet the angels and listen to their reply. you say as-salamu 'alaykum. what do they say?
games.why: they added wa rahmatullah. the first greeting in the story was answered with better (Sahih al-Bukhari).

practice: Think of the last few greetings you received: a text, a hello at the door, a message from a coworker.
Picture answering each one again, a little better: their name, a real wish, and if you greet with salam, the mercy and the blessings added.
